column1: Day 1 | What counts toward the less-than-55-lb limit?
column2: Everything on board or attached at takeoff, including battery and payload.

column1: Day 1 | What is the normal altitude limit?
column2: 400 ft AGL, measured above the ground beneath the aircraft; the structure exception has separate conditions.

column1: Day 1 | What separation is required below clouds?
column2: At least 500 ft below the cloud.

column1: Day 1 | What horizontal cloud separation is required?
column2: At least 2,000 ft horizontally.

column1: Day 1 | What is the maximum groundspeed?
column2: 87 knots, equivalent to 100 mph.

column1: Day 1 | Where is the 3-statute-mile visibility assessed?
column2: From the location of the control station.

column1: Day 1 | Who has final authority over the operation?
column2: The designated remote pilot in command, even when someone else manipulates the controls.

column1: Day 1 | Can a camera feed replace the required unaided view?
column2: No. Visual-line-of-sight requirements still apply; corrective lenses are permitted.

column1: Day 1 | What are the two structure-exception distances?
column2: Within a 400-ft radius of the structure and no higher than 400 ft above its immediate uppermost limit.

column1: Day 1 | Does eight hours since drinking always mean fit to fly?
column2: No. You also must not be under the influence or have a BAC of 0.04 or greater, and must be fit for safe operation.

column1: Day 2 | How do you convert MSL altitude to AGL height?
column2: Subtract terrain elevation MSL directly beneath the aircraft from the aircraft's altitude MSL.

column1: Day 2 | What does 40 over 12 on a Class C shelf mean?
column2: A ceiling of 4,000 ft MSL and floor of 1,200 ft MSL.

column1: Day 2 | What does SFC mean on an airspace floor label?
column2: The airspace begins at the surface.

column1: Day 2 | Which B, C, and D drone operations require authorization?
column2: Operations inside Class B, C, or D require prior ATC authorization under 107.41.

column1: Day 2 | What does a dashed blue boundary usually identify?
column2: Class D airspace. Check its ceiling and effective times.

column1: Day 2 | What does a magenta vignette mean?
column2: Class E starts at 700 ft AGL on the shaded side, unless another airspace designation changes the location.

column1: Day 2 | Which Class E surface designation requires 107.41 authorization?
column2: E2: the surface area designated for an airport. E4 extensions do not independently trigger that requirement.

column1: Day 2 | What is the parenthesized number under an obstacle elevation?
column2: The obstacle's height above ground level; the top number is its elevation MSL.

column1: Day 2 | Does a UAS Facility Map grid value authorize a flight?
column2: No. It supports authorization processing; obtain and follow the actual required approval.

column1: Day 2 | Does Class G mean no flight restrictions apply?
column2: No. Check TFRs, prohibited/restricted areas, airport activity, and all other applicable rules.

column1: Day 3 | Does a 0.40-lb Part 107 drone need registration?
column2: Yes. The small recreational-weight exception does not exempt Part 107 aircraft.

column1: Day 3 | How long is Part 48 drone registration normally valid?
column2: Three years; keep it current and comply with marking and certificate requirements.

column1: Day 3 | What extra visibility rule applies with a Remote ID broadcast module?
column2: The person manipulating the controls must be able to see the aircraft throughout the operation.

column1: Day 3 | What must stay inside a FRIA for its no-equipment option?
column2: Both the aircraft and the person manipulating its controls, with the aircraft seen throughout the operation.

column1: Day 3 | What anti-collision light visibility does normal night flight require?
column2: At least three statute miles, with a flash rate sufficient to avoid a collision; applicable updated testing/training is also required.

column1: Day 3 | Which people category requires an airworthiness certificate?
column2: Category 4. Follow its operating limitations and maintenance requirements as well.

column1: Day 3 | Can Category 3 fly over an open-air assembly?
column2: No. The prohibition covers operation over the assembly, not only sustained flight.

column1: Day 3 | How often must PIC knowledge recency be satisfied?
column2: Within the previous 24 calendar months through an applicable qualifying test or training pathway.

column1: Day 3 | When is a qualifying safety event reported?
column2: To the FAA no later than ten calendar days afterward. Serious injury, loss of consciousness, or qualifying non-drone property damage triggers the rule.

column1: Day 3 | Does airspace authorization waive VLOS?
column2: No. It is a separate approval; a deviation from VLOS needs applicable relief under its own conditions.

column1: Day 4 | What is the difference between a METAR and a TAF?
column2: METAR = observed airport weather. TAF = forecast terminal weather.

column1: Day 4 | Are METAR wind directions true or magnetic?
column2: True north. The direction tells you where the wind comes from.

column1: Day 4 | What does BKN023 mean?
column2: Broken clouds at 2,300 ft above the station. Broken can establish a ceiling.

column1: Day 4 | Which cloud groups establish a ceiling?
column2: The lowest broken or overcast layer, or reported vertical visibility into an obscuration.

column1: Day 4 | What does FM191500 mean in a TAF?
column2: New prevailing conditions beginning on day 19 at 1500 UTC.

column1: Day 4 | What does an inversion commonly do to mixing and visibility?
column2: Suppresses vertical mixing; haze or moisture may become trapped and visibility may worsen.

column1: Day 4 | What distinguishes advection fog?
column2: Moist air moves over a colder surface.

column1: Day 4 | What three ingredients support thunderstorms?
column2: Moisture, unstable air and a lifting mechanism.

column1: Day 4 | What happens to propeller performance as density altitude increases?
column2: It generally decreases because the air is less dense.

column1: Day 4 | Why can a tailwind outbound threaten the return?
column2: The return headwind can require more time and energy. Budget for the return before launching.

column1: Day 5 | Who has final authority over the drone operation?
column2: The designated remote pilot in command.

column1: Day 5 | Name the four preflight environment checks in §107.49.
column2: Weather; airspace and restrictions; people and property; other ground hazards.

column1: Day 5 | Is a visual observer mandatory for every Part 107 flight?
column2: No. If one is used, visual observation, coordination and effective communication requirements apply.

column1: Day 5 | What does IMSAFE check?
column2: Illness, medication, stress, alcohol, fatigue and emotion.

column1: Day 5 | What attitude says “Accidents happen to other people”?
column2: Invulnerability. The antidote is to recognize that it could happen to you.

column1: Day 5 | What does PAVE stand for?
column2: Pilot, Aircraft, enVironment and External pressures.

column1: Day 5 | What is autokinesis?
column2: A stationary point of light can appear to move when stared at in darkness.

column1: Day 5 | When is a written emergency-deviation report required?
column2: When the FAA requests it. Deviations are limited to what the emergency requires.

column1: Day 5 | What must you know about lost-link behavior before launch?
column2: The selected response, home point, return path and altitude, obstacles and power needed to recover safely.

column1: Day 5 | Does Part 107 set one universal battery reserve percentage?
column2: No. Ensure enough available power for the intended flight and plan a suitable margin.

column1: Day 6 | Which frequency is for non-towered airport traffic awareness?
column2: The published CTAF, not the ATIS, ASOS or AWOS weather frequency.

column1: Day 6 | What does a circled C next to a frequency identify?
column2: A common traffic advisory frequency (CTAF).

column1: Day 6 | Does transmitting on CTAF grant permission to enter Class D?
column2: No. Part 107 still requires prior ATC authorization for Class D operation.

column1: Day 6 | What approximate magnetic heading does runway 18 represent?
column2: 180°. The reciprocal runway is 36, approximately 360°.

column1: Day 6 | What traffic-pattern turn direction is standard unless otherwise specified?
column2: Left turns.

column1: Day 6 | What aircraft condition produces especially strong wake vortices?
column2: Heavy, clean and slow.

column1: Day 6 | What is included in the less-than-55-lb takeoff weight?
column2: The aircraft and everything onboard or attached, including battery and payload.

column1: Day 6 | How is center of gravity calculated from weights and moments?
column2: Total moment divided by total weight, using consistent units and datum.

column1: Day 6 | What happens to load factor as bank angle increases in a level turn?
column2: It increases. An ideal coordinated 60° level bank requires 2 G.

column1: Day 6 | Does a clear TFR check establish that controlled-airspace flight is authorized?
column2: No. TFRs and ATC authorization are separate checks.

column1: Day 7 | Cloud base is 900 ft AGL. With ordinary limits, what is the maximum height beneath it?
column2: 400 ft AGL: 900 − 500 = 400, also satisfying the usual 400-ft ceiling.

column1: Day 7 | A Class C shelf says 50 over 20. What is its floor?
column2: 2,000 ft MSL. These charted Class C limits use hundreds of feet MSL.

column1: Day 7 | Which reference does METAR wind use?
column2: True north; the direction is where the wind comes from.

column1: Day 7 | Why can an inversion worsen haze?
column2: Stable air suppresses vertical mixing and can trap pollutants and moisture.

column1: Day 7 | A qualifying test was completed May 10, 2025. When does its 24-calendar-month recency end?
column2: May 31, 2027, unless another qualifying test or training renews recency.

column1: Day 7 | Which operations-over-people category requires an airworthiness certificate?
column2: Category 4.

column1: Day 7 | Can Category 3 operations fly over an open-air assembly?
column2: No. Category 3 prohibits operations over open-air assemblies.

column1: Day 7 | What does the required UAG passing mark mean numerically?
column2: At least 42 correct out of 60 scored questions. Five additional questions are unscored.

column1: Day 7 | What causes a fixed-wing aircraft to stall?
column2: Exceeding the wing’s critical angle of attack. There is no single stall speed for every weight, bank, and configuration.

column1: Day 7 | How long after a permanent mailing-address change can a pilot exercise certificate privileges without notifying the FAA?
column2: Up to 30 days. After that, the pilot cannot exercise the privileges until the FAA has been notified of the address change.
